top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu) is the only configuration on the slate and I judge it clearly preferable to no award. The case rests on the common criteria rather than on the unanimous round-2 support, which is not evidence of merit. His voice is distinctive at the level of the sentence and the whole book. Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known, sustain a formal architecture at very large scale in which memory, the body and dream become a single metaphysical project rather than decoration. The poetry and shorter prose appear to belong to the same project, which supports a whole-oeuvre citation naming prose as the core and poetry as its ground, without national or regional framing. The reservations remain: I cannot assess Romanian sentence rhythm and wordplay independently of translation, no member has verified whether the later long novels deepen or only extend the early project, and translation coverage of the poetry and essays is thinner. How the will's reference to an idealistic tendency applies to an inward, encyclopedic and often disturbing project is an interpretive question that I do not treat as settled, though serious, sustained inquiry into consciousness, memory and mortality is arguably within its scope. These limits are shared by all members, so agreement is weak corroboration. They are not strong enough to prefer no award. This judgment rests on public knowledge and reception, not independent reading of the originals.
